source: Canadian National Autism Foundation, cnaf.net/provinceres.html; each entry checked on its own website

entries.name: Preschool Autism Program (Education and Early Childhood Development)
entries.description: New Brunswick government program that gives preschool children diagnosed with autism intervention based on Applied Behaviour Analysis, delivered by VIVA Therapeutic Services at home, in child care or at VIVA's regional offices, in English or French. Families get either intensive direct intervention or lower-intensity consultative intervention, with parent coaching, until the child starts school.
entries.cost_note: The page does not mention fees; VIVA delivers the services under a contract with the province.
entries.evidence: The New Brunswick Preschool Autism Program provides evidence-based intervention services to preschool children who are diagnosed with Autism Spectrum Disorder.
entries.notes: CNAF lists this program twice (Government and Services sections, both old services_renderer.13836 URLs, still the page gnb.ca links to). The page loads its text from a separate fragment (serviceinfo.13836.ttl.html), fetched for the quote and contacts. To enrol, the diagnosing professional sends a Confirmation of Diagnosis form to the department; the child must be diagnosed between ages 0 and 5 and not yet in school. The email is the program's shared inbox.

entries.name: Family Supports for Children with Disabilities (Department of Social Development)
entries.description: New Brunswick program that helps families meet the unmet needs of a child with a disability, for example medical equipment and transportation, relief care, home support, child care aides and family support workers. Families work with a social worker and can choose social-worker-managed services or family-managed services with the funds paid to the family.
entries.cost_note: Families who have the means make a financial contribution towards services.
entries.evidence: The Family Supports for Children with Disabilities Program assists families to address the unmet needs of the child or children with the disability by providing the required support and resources.
entries.notes: CNAF links to the old www2.gnb.ca page (services_renderer.10195), which now says it is no longer updated and points to gnb.ca's Persons with disabilities page; this is the program's current page. Families can self-refer by phone, or a professional can refer them.

entries.name: Healthy Smiles, Clear Vision (Department of Social Development)
entries.description: New Brunswick dental and vision plan for children 18 and under in low-income families, covering basic dental care (exams, X-rays, extractions and preventive treatments) and basic vision care (a yearly exam, lenses and frames). Families must be under the income limits, have no other dental or vision coverage, and enrol their children in the federal Canadian Dental Care Plan for full coverage.
entries.cost_note: Government plan for eligible children; the page does not mention any fee.
entries.evidence: Healthy Smiles, Clear Vision is New Brunswick’s dental and vision plan for children of low-income families.
entries.notes: CNAF listed it under "Dental Care". The phone is Medavie Blue Cross, which answers questions about the plan; application forms go by mail or fax to Healthy Smiles, Clear Vision, 644 Main Street, Moncton. Children already covered through Social Development are moved to the plan automatically. The income limits on the page are based on June 2025 figures.

entries.name: New Brunswick Prescription Drug Program (NBPDP) – Children in care and special needs children
entries.description: Prescription drug coverage under the New Brunswick Prescription Drug Program for children in the care of the Minister of Social Development and for special needs children, with eligibility decided by the Department of Social Development. Drugs listed in the New Brunswick Formulary are covered.
entries.cost_note: The page says there are no fees or co-payments associated with this plan.
entries.evidence: Children in care of the Minister of Social Development and special needs children are eligible for drug coverage through this plan.
entries.notes: CNAF links to the old "Plan G" page (services_renderer.8896), which returns 404; the plan is now described on the NBPDP eligibility page. The phone is New Brunswick Drug Plans, toll free within NB (1-506-867-4515 otherwise).

entries.name: Student Aid for students with disabilities (Student Financial Services, New Brunswick)
entries.description: New Brunswick's Student Financial Services runs federal and provincial student aid, with extra support for post-secondary students with a permanent or persistent disability. This includes the Canada Student Grant for Students with Disabilities, the Canada Student Grant for Services and Equipment (for tutors, note-takers, interpreters and technical aids) and full-time aid with a reduced course load.
entries.cost_note: Loans must be repaid while grants and bursaries do not; the pages do not mention any fee to apply.
entries.evidence: Students with disabilities can receive up to a maximum of $20,000 per academic year to purchase education related services and assistive equipment which are not provided by their educational institution.
entries.notes: CNAF links to the old Student Financial Services page (404) and the old Canada Student Grant for Services and Equipment page on www2.gnb.ca, which now says it is no longer updated and points to the Student Aid page. Students must self-identify, send the Disability Verification Form and, for a learning disability, a psychoeducational assessment done within five years. Applications go through the NB Student Aid Portal.

entries.name: New Brunswick Human Rights Commission
entries.description: Provincial commission that deals with discrimination under the New Brunswick Human Rights Act. People who experience discrimination in New Brunswick can contact it and file a complaint, and it also gives free human rights training and workshops and publishes guides, including one on requesting accommodations at work.
entries.cost_note: Its human rights training and workshops are free; the pages do not mention a fee to file a complaint.
entries.address: 751 Brunswick Street Fredericton, New Brunswick E3B 1H8
entries.evidence: If you experience discrimination in New Brunswick, you can contact the Commission and file a complaint.
entries.notes: CNAF links to gnb.ca/hrc-cdp/index-e.asp, which still answered 522 (origin timeout) after --force; the Commission's current site is on www2.gnb.ca. Contact details are from its gnb.ca contact listing (Barry House; reception (506) 453-2301); its email address is hidden by the site's email protection.

entries.name: Inclusion NB
entries.description: Provincial organisation for people with intellectual and developmental disabilities and their families, known for decades as the New Brunswick Association for Community Living. It supports inclusive education from early learning to post-secondary, including help with transitions and case management for post-secondary students aged 18 to 30, and also works on family support, employment and advocacy.
entries.cost_note: The site does not mention cost.
entries.address: 984 Prospect Street, Unit A Fredericton, NB E3B 2T8
entries.evidence: Inclusion NB works with early learning centres, public schools, and post-secondary institutions to provide seamless and successful transitions for children and youth with an intellectual or developmental disability.
entries.notes: CNAF links to an NBACL tip sheet on personalized learning plans (nbacl.nb.ca), which timed out; the New Brunswick Association for Community Living changed its name to Inclusion NB in 2022 and now uses inclusionnb.ca. The main office is in Fredericton, with other offices around the province; it also runs an online learning platform (Inclusive Communities Institute).

entries.name: Pediatric Neurodevelopmental Service (Stan Cassidy Centre for Rehabilitation, Horizon Health Network)
entries.description: Provincial team at the Stan Cassidy Centre in Fredericton that supports children and youth 17 and under with severe neurodevelopmental impairment, including the most complex forms of autism, by consulting with and assisting their families, local therapists and schools. Referrals come from a pediatrician, neurologist, physiatrist or psychiatrist, or from local clinicians, and the team does not provide direct therapy.
entries.cost_note: The site does not mention cost.
entries.address: 800 Priestman Street Fredericton, New Brunswick, E3B 0C7
entries.evidence: We are an interdisciplinary team of professionals who work together to support children and youth with a complex neurodevelopmental disorder by working collaboratively with local clinicians.
entries.notes: CNAF links to the old stancassidy.ca "Paediatric Autism Rehabilitation Services" page, which now redirects to Horizon's Stan Cassidy Centre page; autism services are now part of the Pediatric Neurodevelopmental Service. Services are in English and French, on site, as outpatient visits or by outreach. The main page lists the Pediatric Neurodevelopmental services line as (506) 452-5784.

entries.name: Speech-Language Pathology (Horizon Health Network)
entries.description: Public speech-language pathology services from Horizon Health Network for children from birth to school entry and for adults, at hospitals and health centres in the Fredericton, Miramichi, Moncton, Saint John and Upper River Valley areas. School-age children get speech-language services through their school district instead.
entries.cost_note: The page does not mention cost.
entries.evidence: Speech-Language Pathologists at Horizon Health Network work with children from birth to school entry and adults.
entries.notes: CNAF links to an old horizonnb.ca .aspx page that returns 404; this is Horizon's current Speech-Language Pathology page. Booking numbers are by area (e.g. Moncton and Sackville 1-833-944-0860, Fredericton and Upper River Valley 1-833-928-2070, Saint John 506-648-6255), so no single phone is given. In some communities the service is provided by Vitalité Health Network.

entries.name: Speech-Language Pathology (Vitalité Health Network)
entries.description: Public speech-language pathology services from Vitalité Health Network for people with communication, feeding or swallowing difficulties: preschoolers, school-aged children with specific needs, and adults. Speech-language pathologists assess, give therapy and coach the people who communicate with the patient, in inpatient and outpatient settings.
entries.cost_note: The page does not mention cost.
entries.evidence: The Speech-Language Pathology Department provides inpatient and outpatient services to people with communication differences/difficulties (e.g., speech, language, voice), feeding difficulties, and swallowing difficulties.
entries.notes: CNAF links to vitalitenb.ca/en/service-points/speech-language-pathology, which now redirects to a 404 page; this is the current page in Vitalité's service directory. Phones are by zone: Beauséjour 506-862-4000, Northwest 506-739-2200, Restigouche 506-789-5000, Acadie-Bathurst 506-544-3000; the email is hidden by email protection. For school-aged children the page lists only specific needs (feeding/swallowing, resonance and voice).

entries.name: Ruth Woodworth SLP
entries.description: Private speech-language pathology practice in Fredericton for children, adolescents and adults with speech, language or communication challenges, and their families. Services include assessments, short-term consultation, weekly therapy and Hanen training for early childhood educators, with clients seen at the office or where they are.
entries.cost_note: Phone or email consultation is free; the site does not list fees for assessment or therapy.
entries.evidence: Ruth's private practice in speech-language pathology serves children, adolescents, and adults who are facing challenges in speech, language and/or communication, and their families.
entries.notes: The site looks old (design credit ©2008, no dates anywhere), so confirm the practice is still open before publishing. The only email on the site is Ruth's own, so it is left out.

entries.name: Metro Hearing and Speech
entries.description: Private audiology and speech-language pathology centre in Moncton for children and adults. Its speech-language pathologist assesses and treats articulation, motor speech, language comprehension and expression, and stuttering, and the centre also tests for auditory processing disorders.
entries.cost_note: A private practice; the site does not list fees.
entries.address: 1688 Mountain Road, Suite 201 Moncton, NB, Canada, E1G 1A6
entries.evidence: If you or a family member experience any of the following challenges, our speech-language pathologist (SLP) is ready to help:
entries.notes: CNAF lists it as Metro Sound & Speech; the site (still at metrosoundandspeech.com) now calls it Metro Hearing and Speech. Its email address is hidden by email protection. People can book their own appointment or be referred by a professional.

entries.name: Clinique Orthophonie Chaleur (Chaleur Speech-Language Pathology Clinic)
entries.description: Private speech-language pathology clinic in Bathurst, with a second office in Caraquet, that assesses and treats spoken and written language delays and disorders, articulation, voice problems, stuttering and swallowing difficulties in children and adults.
entries.cost_note: The site does not mention fees.
entries.address: 1025 rue Ste Anne - Suite A Bathurst, N.-B. E2A 6X1
entries.evidence: nous avons étendu nos services pour venir en aide à une population variée, que ce soit auprès des enfants ou des adultes.
entries.notes: CNAF lists this clinic without a website (only the speech-language pathologist's personal Gmail); its own site, orthophoniechaleur.ca, matches CNAF's Bathurst address and phone. The site is in French (its English version says "coming soon"). Caraquet office: 258 boul. St-Pierre Ouest - Suite C, same phone.

entries.name: Autism Resource Centre (Greater Moncton)
entries.description: Community centre in Moncton for autistic people of all ages, their families and caregivers, and professionals, that helps people reach resources, information and services. Its work covers education and training, awareness, resources and referrals, and supports and social activities, which need registration a week ahead.
entries.cost_note: The site does not mention cost.
entries.evidence: The Autism Resource Centre is committed to assisting in the accessing of resources, information, and services.
entries.notes: CNAF links to monctonarc.com, which now shows an anti-bot check (403); the centre now uses autismresource.ca, the website NB EECD's Autism Resource Hub gives for "Autism Resource Centre Inc. (Moncton region)". The home page gives a new address at 107 Cameron Street (the History page still mentions Riverview) and says new programs are being developed.

entries.name: Hébert Individualized Learning Services (HILS) (Centre Hébert Center)
entries.description: Private agency at the Hébert Centre in Dieppe that offers consultation, assessment and individualized services to people of all ages with social, language, learning and behavioural challenges, using trauma-informed Applied Behavioural Analysis (ABA). Goals can cover communication, behaviour, academics, life skills and leisure, and it serves the Greater Moncton and Saint John areas.
entries.cost_note: The site offers a free consultation; it does not list fees for services.
entries.evidence: Hébert Individualized Learning Services (HILS) is a private agency that offers collaborative consultation, assessment, individualized services, and supports to people of all ages with social, language, learning, and behavioural challenges.
entries.notes: From CNAF's Hébert Centre listing: hebertcentre.ca now lists HILS, the Safari Social daycare and Hébert Well-Being counselling at 55 Englehart Street, Dieppe. CNAF also lists Hébert Family Support Services (hfss.ca, which timed out); HILS offers similar services at the same address but the site does not say it replaced HFSS.

entries.name: Centre de l'Autisme du Restigouche (Restigouche Autism Center)
entries.description: Non-profit autism centre in Campbellton, founded by parents and professionals, for families and caregivers of children with autism in the Restigouche region. It runs parent support groups, information sessions and workshops, points families to professional resources, and has a resource library of books, toys, games and software such as Boardmaker.
entries.cost_note: The site does not mention fees; printing, laminating and binding are offered at cost price.
entries.evidence: We offer support groups for parents, information sessions and workshops, as well as guidance to professional ressources available in our region.
entries.notes: The centre is in Room 253 of Polyvalente Roland-Pépin; postal address P.O. Box 1942, Atholville, NB E3N 4E4. The phone is printed without its area code (506). https://www.carac.ca has a certificate problem, so the http pages are used; the email is the centre's general address.

entries.name: M.O.R.E. Services, Inc.
entries.description: Not-for-profit agency in Miramichi that supports individuals with intellectual disabilities through vocational and life skills programs and community residential services. Programs include life, social and safety skills, employment readiness training, on-the-job training and support, and recreational activities, including work in its garden centre.
entries.cost_note: The site does not mention fees; services are reached through the Department of Social Development.
entries.evidence: M.O.R.E. Services, Inc. is a not-for profit agency in Miramichi, New Brunswick, which assists and supports individuals with intellectual disabilities.
entries.notes: To get services, people contact the Department of Social Development's regional office; the agency can be called for information. Mailing address P.O. Box 69, Station A, Miramichi, NB E1N 3A6. The email is the agency's general address.
